title: Rego Foundations
subtitle: Packages, default-deny, allow-if, input vs data
content:
📦 Package, Input, Data: The Three Namespaces

A Rego policy declares a package (its API path: package demo → /v1/data/demo), reads the per-request input document, and reads slowly-changing data (roles, team memberships) loaded separately. Rules define allow; anything undefined is denied when you set the default.

Rego 1.x: canonical sidecar shape (default-deny + three allow rules) 
# Last verified: 2026-09 against OPA docs + rest-rego sidecar pattern
package policies

# Deny by default (fail-closed). NEVER default allow := true.
default allow := false

# Allow listed applications (JWT claim from the sidecar input)
allow if {
    input.jwt.appid == "11112222-3333-4444-5555-666677778888"
}

# Allow based on roles
allow if {
    "admin" in input.jwt.roles
}

# Allow public endpoints without auth context.
# Narrow by design: GET only, exact allowlisted paths. A bare
# path[0] == "public" check would also allow PUT/DELETE under /public/*
# (including future non-idempotent endpoints) — every carve-out gets
# its own deny-test (Lesson 20).
allow if {
    input.request.method == "GET"
    input.request.path in [["public", "health"], ["public", "version"]]
}
# Last verified: 2026-09 against OPA docs + rest-rego sidecar pattern package policies # Deny by default (fail-closed). NEVER default allow := true. default allow := false # Allow listed applications (JWT claim from the sidecar input) allow if { input.jwt.appid == "11112222-3333-4444-5555-666677778888" } # Allow based on roles allow if { "admin" in input.jwt.roles } # Allow public endpoints without auth context. # Narrow by design: GET only, exact allowlisted paths. A bare # path[0] == "public" check would also allow PUT/DELETE under /public/* # (including future non-idempotent endpoints) — every carve-out gets # its own deny-test (Lesson 20). allow if { input.request.method == "GET" input.request.path in [["public", "health"], ["public", "version"]] }

🔑 Critical Review: What the Docs and Repos Agree On

  • OPA official docs: default allow := false is the documented deny-by-default idiom; without it a missing field yields undefined, which most integrations treat as deny — but explicit false is auditable and testable.
  • rest-rego (GitHub): production sidecar uses exactly this shape — package policies, input.jwt.* claims, public-path carve-out, hot reload, <5ms overhead. Our example mirrors its policies/request.rego.
  • Rego 1.x note: modern syntax is allow if { ... } (no = true needed). Older allow { ... } still parses but the if keyword is current.

🧪 Evaluate Locally (No Server)

OPA eval: the unit-test loop for policy 
# Score one decision file against policy, like CI does:
opa eval -i input.json -d request.rego 'data.policies.allow'

# NOTE the shape difference: the REST decision API wraps the runtime
# request under an "input" key ({"input": {...}}), but 'opa eval -i'
# loads the file AS the input document itself — no wrapper. Wrapping
# here would make rules see input.input.* and deny everything in CI
# while the playground (which wraps) still allows.
{ "jwt": { "appid": "11112222-3333-4444-5555-666677778888",
           "roles": ["viewer"] },
  "request": { "method": "GET", "path": ["public", "health"] } }
# expect: { "result": [{ "expressions": [{ "value": true }] }] }
# Score one decision file against policy, like CI does: opa eval -i input.json -d request.rego 'data.policies.allow' # NOTE the shape difference: the REST decision API wraps the runtime # request under an "input" key ({"input": {...}}), but 'opa eval -i' # loads the file AS the input document itself — no wrapper. Wrapping # here would make rules see input.input.* and deny everything in CI # while the playground (which wraps) still allows. { "jwt": { "appid": "11112222-3333-4444-5555-666677778888", "roles": ["viewer"] }, "request": { "method": "GET", "path": ["public", "health"] } } # expect: { "result": [{ "expressions": [{ "value": true }] }] }

⚠️ Beginner Traps

  • Undefined ≠ false: without a default, a typo'd field name silently denies. Good for security, miserable for debugging — add deny_reason helpers (Lesson 11).
  • in needs Rego 1.x / future.keywords import on old OPA: pin your OPA version in CI (Lesson 20).
  • Input shape is a contract: document it; the PEP and the policy must agree, or rules silently miss.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Pick the three Rego scenarios and confirm which allow-rule (if any) fires. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: What does default allow := false do in a Rego policy?

options.text: Makes unmatched requests evaluate to false (deny) instead of undefined

questions.explanation: OPA docs prescribe default for deny-by-default: explicit false is auditable and testable, vs undefined which integrations merely coerce to deny.

questions.question: package policies in request.rego maps to which OPA API path?

options.text: There is no mapping; packages are comments

questions.explanation: OPA converts the package path to the data API path — the convention the REST-demo repos rely on when POSTing decisions.

questions.question: Where do per-request JWT claims belong, vs role tables?

options.text: Claims in input (per request); role tables in data (loaded separately, updated via API)
Both hard-coded in the Rego file
Claims in data, role tables in input

questions.explanation: input = dynamic per-request; data = slowly-changing context injected via /v1/data PUT/PATCH. Mixing them up breaks caching and hot updates.

questions.question: A request from an unknown appid to /private/report gets allow=true. First suspect?

options.text: A fail-open default (default allow := true) or an over-broad allow rule
The JWT expiry timestamp (an authN fact, not the authZ decision)
The number of allow rules in the file (more rules do not mean safer)

questions.explanation: Unexpected allows trace to the default or to a rule matching more than intended (e.g. path[0] checks without method checks). Deny-tests catch both.

questions.question: How do you unit-test a Rego rule without running a server?

options.text: You cannot; a server is mandatory
By opening the file in a browser
By emailing it to the OPA team

questions.explanation: opa eval is the documented fast loop and the basis of opa test suites in CI (Lesson 20).

questions.question: Two teams deploy packages both named acme.payments. What breaks?

options.text: Bundle collision — identical data-API paths; namespace packages per team/service
Nothing — OPA merges same-named packages safely

questions.explanation: Package names are API paths. Collisions silently merge or shadow rules — namespace like code.

questions.question: Group membership changes must take effect within a minute, with no redeploy. Where does membership live?

options.text: In data (PUT/PATCH at runtime); policy reads it, bundle untouched

questions.explanation: Input/data separation exists for exactly this: fast-moving facts ride in data, slow-moving logic in versioned policy.

questions.question: opa eval returns undefined for data.policies.allow on a request you expect allowed. First check?

options.text: No rule body matched the input (or default missing) — print the input, diff against rule conditions

questions.explanation: Undefined means unmatched, not broken. Debugging starts with the input document, not the engine.
